Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the StratoCore Technologies Q2 FY24 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. If using a speakerphone, please pick up the handset before pressing the keys. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing StratoCore Technologies's results for the Q2 FY24. With me on the call are Sarah Chen, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Patel, Chief Financial Officer; and Lisa Wong, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. StratoCore Technologies had a strong Q2, driven by continued growth in our cloud platform and increasing adoption of our AI-powered services.

During the quarter, we focused on four key areas:
1. Expanding our global infrastructure.
2. Enhancing our platform security.
3. Driving innovation in AI and machine learning.
4. Strengthening our partnerships.

Let me elaborate on our global infrastructure expansion, which is pivotal as we scale to meet surging demand for AI and machine learning workloads, much like those powering generative AI models from leading innovators. This remains the cornerstone of our long-term growth strategy in the cloud computing space, targeting a massive AI infrastructure opportunity exceeding $200 billion. We're raising our FY2024 capital expenditure guidance to $11.5 billion to $12.5 billion, up from the previous $10 billion to $11 billion range. This adjustment accounts for hyperscale buildouts and investments in high-density GPU clusters. Q2 CapEx reached $2.9 billion, or 28% of revenue, aligning with our stepped-up profile and up 45% year-over-year due to AI capacity deployments. We anticipate Q4 peaking at $3.2 billion, then normalizing to 18-22% of revenue in FY2025 as utilization improves.

We're adding 1.2 gigawatts of IT capacity globally by year-end, expanding our portfolio beyond 5.5 GW. This involves 12 new hyperscale facilities coming online or starting construction, plus 8 expansions in current sites. Our newest sites support 100-120 kW per rack, a big leap from legacy 40-60 kW, ideal for NVIDIA H100 and Blackwell GPU clusters handling trillion-parameter large language models.

Breaking it down regionally: In the Americas, 55% of new CapEx, we've activated two 200 MW campuses in Northern Virginia—our premier East Coast hub—and started a 300 MW liquid-cooled site in Phoenix. Virginia now holds 25% of global capacity, optimized for low-latency inference for finance and healthcare clients, with 92% utilization and 60% quarter-over-quarter AI workload growth.

EMEA gets 30% of CapEx, focusing on sovereign cloud and GDPR needs. Phase 1 of Frankfurt-3 (150 MW) is complete with zoned isolation, and a 100 MW edge site in Milan supports Italy's AI startups. Sustainability is key: PUE under 1.25 using renewables and liquid cooling. A partnership with Ørsted secures 500 MW offshore wind, covering 80% of needs by 2026. Utilization is 88%, with 35% capacity growth.

APAC, 15% of CapEx, emphasizes proximity amid geopolitical shifts. Singapore-2 added 120 MW for trading and telcos with sub-10ms latency. A 250 MW build in Jakarta targets Southeast Asia's $15 billion market, and $800 million in Tokyo edge clusters aligns with Japan's AI efforts. Utilization is 85%, heading to 95% by mid-2025.

On the tech side, 70% of new capacity uses direct-to-chip liquid cooling, cutting energy 30% for high-power racks and doubling density. Our Nexara Fabric (800Gbps RDMA-oCE) reduces training latency 25%. Power efficiency is up 50% to 1.8x via AI orchestration for hybrid x86/ARM. Global PUE improved to 1.18 from 1.22 year-over-year, with 65% renewables—aiming for 100% by 2030.

This positions us ahead in AI, with an asset-light model blending owned sites and partners like Equinix for better ROIC. New capacity hits 85% utilization in 12 months, delivering 25-30% IRR on AI builds. Backed by IDC's 40% AI cloud CAGR forecast, we've secured 80% power PPAs and modular designs slashing deployment time.

Now I'll turn the call over to Mike Patel to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we had a strong financial performance in the Q2. Revenue grew by 28% year-over-year to $3.8 billion. Our gross margin was 74%, and our operating margin was 32%.

Turning to average revenue per user—or ARPU—a vital metric highlighting our customer expansion and monetization in our multi-tenant platform. We calculate ARPU as quarterly revenue divided by average active accounts, annualized. For Q2 FY24, ARPU hit $34,750, up 21% year-over-year from $28,720 and 6% sequentially from $32,780, beating our 18-20% guidance amid AI and digital transformation surges. Trailing 12-month ARPU is $33,200, up 19%, strong versus peers like Snowflake and Datadog.

By segment: Enterprise (ACV >$1M), 28% of accounts but 62% revenue, ARPU at $162,400—up 27%—driven by IaaS and S3-compatible storage migrations, with 128% NRR from upsells to StratoGenAI, scaling to production inference.

Mid-market/SMB (72% accounts, 38% revenue) ARPU rose to $24,600, +16%, with 2.7x expansions via serverless StratoFunctions and Kubernetes-based StratoOrchestrator, holding 15% APM share per Gartner.

By vertical: Compute/storage ARPU up 19% to $18,200; Data & AI soared 32% to $52,300, as a Fortune 100 retailer grew RPO 40% with StratoVector embeddings on Llama 3, cutting costs 35%.

Regionally: North America (65% revenue) $41,200 (+20%), aided by sovereignty rules; EMEA (18%) $29,800 (+24%) via StratoSecure and DAX wins; APAC (12%) $22,500 (+18%), boosted by Tokyo/Mumbai sovereign clouds and StratoHybrid Bridge.

Drivers: AI innovation (45% expansions to StratoGenAI, 28% TCO cuts); Reserved Capacity Marketplace (utilization 62% to 78%, +12% ARPU); partnerships with Salesforce Einstein/ServiceNow (+35% co-sell ARR).

Q3 ARPU guidance: $36,000-$37,500 (22-25% YoY), backed by $2.1B RPO up 31%, 92% current. Cohort NRR 125%, gross retention 95%. Piloting AI metering for 10-15% FY25 lift. This signals robust health in a $1.4T market by 2027, 30% AI CAGR.

Now, I'll hand it back to Sarah for further comments.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Mike. We are particularly excited about the momentum we are seeing with StratoAI, which is driving significant workload expansions and cost savings for our customers.

Let me discuss customer churn and retention trends, a cornerstone metric in cloud where retention fuels our model, given high switching costs for AI/ML inference, Kubernetes containers, and object storage data lakes. Net revenue retention—or NRR—is our stickiness gauge.

For Q2 FY24 ending June 30, annualized logo churn was 4.2%, down 180 bps from 6.0% in Q2 FY23—our lowest in three years, beating IDC's 7-8% hyperscaler average. Dollar revenue churn was 3.1%, showing expansions. Gross dollar retention 112%, NRR 122% up from 115% YoY.

Top-tier (> $1M ARR) hit 128% NRR from StratoAI and NitroEdge upsells. Mid-market ($100K-$1M) 118%; SMB 105% from self-service console.

Enterprise (Fortune 1000, 68% ARR) logo churn 2.8%, with 36-month commitments, 95% renewals, boosted by VMware migrations. Developer cohort 6.5%, normalized post-AI hype.

Eight-quarter downtrend from 7.2% peak in Q4 FY22, via Customer Success 2.0 (FinOps engineers, 15-20% TCO savings, 25% renewal boost), zero-egress S3 transfers, GraphQL observability for proactive EKS-like scaling.

Regionally: North America (52% ARR) 3.5% churn, AI-driven (40% expansions GPU H100-equivalent); EMEA (28%) 4.8% from 6.5%, Frankfurt sovereign cloud wins banks; APAC (20%) 5.1%, Singapore/Tokyo expansions yield 135% NRR from Japanese shifts.

Targets: sub-4% Q4 churn. Initiatives: AI-native loops (StratoForge LLM in VPCs, 3x growth); partner lock-in (Snowflake/Databricks, +30% expansions); pricing at 60% RCIs savings; StratoConnect for Azure Arc/Anthos, converting 65% risks to expansions.

FY24 NRR 120-125%, churn <4%, resilient mix (45% AI/ML, 30% storage/compute, 25% SaaS/PaaS) vs. SMB macro, APAC tensions. Gartner 25% AI spend CAGR aids.

We continue to invest in research and development to stay ahead of the curve in the rapidly evolving cloud landscape. Our commitment to innovation is reflected in our recent advancements in zero-trust security architecture.

On that note, let's review key assumptions for our revenue and profitability forecasts, grounding our robust outlook: FY2024 revenue up 28% to $145 billion, adjusted op margins +300 bps to 32%, based on telemetry from 2.5M customers, $220B RPO +42% YoY, GenAI tailwinds.

Revenue pillars: IaaS/PaaS 65% mix, 32% growth from migrations/hybrid.

Customer metrics: 118% NRR (105% existing expansions via Nitro Enclaves confidential compute, Graviton4 25% price-perf); 15K net new enterprises +20% via StratoBedrock; 1.2x usage elasticity, 150% QoQ inference.

AI: $12B run-rate (+$4B accel), GPU supply 85% covered + Trainium2 40% savings; 50% agentic/fine-tuning growth, 35% top-1K adoption.

Regions: Americas 55% (30% growth), sovereign gov cloud; EMEA 25% (25%), €10B AI contracts; APAC 20% (40%), Japan/Korea/India sovereign RPO 2x.

Pricing: 2-3% ASP inflation AI, 15% storage volume; no GCP pressure.

Sensitivities: -5pt NRR -$6B; +10% AI +$8B.

Profitability: 38% EBITDA, CoR 28% (-200bps).

Gross: 74% margins, 85% utilization 120 zones; renewables 60%, $0.07/kWh; custom silicon 35% mix 30% savings; 90% rack fulfillment.

OpEx: S&M 18%, R&D 12% zero-trust/Outposts 25% attach; G&A 4%; $18B SBC.

CapEx: 18% peak ($26B) AI builds, trough 12% FY25, $40B FCF 28% margins, DSO 45, 10% efficiency.

Macro: recession-proof $700B market 22% CAGR; FX neutral; CHIPS/EU AI tailwinds.

Risks: GPU shortages (AMD hedge), AI ROI delay (-150bps margins). $220B RPO de-risks.

This affirms our $1T cloud leadership, AI accelerant, $50B buyback.

With that, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question, please press star one. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Ben Smith:
Thanks, Sarah. Great quarter. Can you expand on how the AI workload growth is influencing your long-term NRR assumptions, especially with the competitive landscape?

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, Ben. Absolutely, AI is a massive driver for our NRR, as we've seen with expansions into StratoAI suites. Our assumptions hold NRR steady in the 120% range, supported by high stickiness in GPU-accelerated training and inference. Competition is there, but our price-performance and integrations like StratoForge keep us ahead, converting trials to multi-year commitments. We're confident in sustained expansion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
Hi team, congrats on the results. On the CapEx front, with the raise to $12.5B max, how are you thinking about returns and utilization timelines given power constraints industry-wide?

Mike Patel:
Thanks, Emily. Our CapEx is laser-focused on high-IRR AI capacity, projecting 85% utilization within 12 months and 25-30% returns. We've locked 80% PPAs, renewables ramp, and liquid cooling for efficiency. Supply chains are stable, and our modular approach speeds deployment. This fuels 25%+ CAGR without compromising margins.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel:
Thanks. Lisa, could you speak to the tech advancements in your Nexara Fabric and how it's supporting distributed AI training versus peers?

Lisa Wong:
Sure, Raj. Nexara Fabric at 800Gbps RDMA-oCE cuts tail latency 25% for training, outperforming standard Ethernet in distributed setups. Integrated with our hybrid ARM/x86, it handles trillion-param models efficiently, giving customers better TCO than competitors. Early adopters are seeing 2x throughput gains.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Great, thanks. Mike or Sarah, with ARPU up 21%, how sustainable is that amid potential SMB slowdowns, and any updates on pricing discipline?

Sarah Chen:
Hi David. ARPU sustainability comes from enterprise depth—128% NRR there—and AI upsells across board. SMB is improving via self-service, and our 60% RCI discounts hold premiums without churn risk. $2.1B RPO visibility confirms trajectory, even in macro caution.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for your questions and your continued support. We are confident in our ability to continue to deliver strong results and create long-term value for our shareholders.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
